sources.entry: Mac Sai - Free, open-source CleanMyMac alternative built with Swift 6 and SwiftUI. Smart Scan, junk cleanup, malware scanner, uninstaller with leftover detection, Space Lens treemap, duplicates, and a live menu bar monitor.

summary.one_liner: Mac Sai is a free, open-source, Swift 6 and SwiftUI Mac cleaner and optimizer that bundles junk cleanup, a signature-based malware scanner, an uninstaller, disk treemap, duplicate finder, and a menu-bar system monitor.
summary.what_it_does: Mac Sai provides 22 modules grouped into Cleanup, Protection, Performance, Applications, and Files, plus a separate menu-bar widget. Cleanup covers a one-click Smart Scan, System Junk across 16+ categories, Universal Binary thinning via lipo, Trash emptying, build-folder cleanup for projects, and Docker and Xcode simulator pruning. Protection includes a malware scanner at Quick, Balanced, and Deep depths that matches Apple XProtect hashes and an optional MalwareBazaar feed, plus browser privacy cleaning that never touches Safari bookmarks. The Applications module offers an uninstaller that searches 17+ Library subdirectories for leftovers and a Reset to Defaults option, along with unused-app detection and an updater that reads Sparkle feeds. Files tools include a squarified-treemap disk visualizer, large and old file finder, duplicate detection with APFS clone consolidation, and a secure shredder. The README says deletions go to the Trash by default, with a protected-paths blocklist and a dry-run mode.
use_cases: clean up junk and caches on a Mac
uninstall an app and its leftover files
scan a Mac for malware or adware
find what is taking up disk space
remove duplicate files and reclaim space with APFS clones
monitor CPU, memory, disk and battery from the menu bar
clear browser history and cookies without touching bookmarks
free space taken by Docker and Xcode simulators
how_to_run: Or download the latest DMG from the project's Releases page and drag Mac Sai to Applications
git clone the repository, then cd MacSai
bash scripts/build-dmg.sh (builds a local, unsigned DMG)
notable: Ships a separate XPC privileged helper, with the kernel enforcing a code-signing requirement on connections
Verification section gives shell commands to check the installed binary for networking classes and compiled-in URLs
Duplicate finder uses APFS copy-on-write clones to reclaim space without deleting any copy
Malware scanner matches exact hashes against Apple XProtect signatures on the Mac, offline
Claims zero telemetry and notarization by Apple; README says the app is not an antivirus
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later, per the comparison table, and the Swift 6 toolchain (Xcode 16+) to build from source
Malware scanning is signature-based and the README states it is not an antivirus; some modules need Full Disk Access
The optional MalwareBazaar feed requires the user to obtain and add their own abuse.ch Auth-Key
keywords: free up disk space on mac
